thread:
sam.greene: Quick share — did a short bringup bench across regions comparing FlashAttention v2, v3, and Triton vendor libraries on H100 pools (us-west & eu-west). Link with full charts: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/bench/kernel-thresholds

jess.lee: nice, TL;DR? :eyes:

sam.greene: TL;DR: v3 gives best p95 for long sequences (>=1024) and better single-request latency for streaming. But in q8-int8 runs on short sequences (<128) we see 5-12% throughput regression vs Triton vendor kernels. Also noticed larger cold-start jitter in apac region.

kai.zheng: can you paste the key numbers?

sam.greene: sure — pasted minimal table below (median latency ms / tokens/s throughput):
```
region | model | q | batch=1 (med) | p95 | throughput (batch=8)
us-west | flashv3 | q8 | 38 | 120 | 350
us-west | flashv2 | q8 | 42 | 150 | 320
us-west | triton-vendor | q8 | 36 | 140 | 390
eu-west | flashv3 | q8 | 40 | 130 | 340
eu-west | triton-vendor | q8 | 35 | 155 | 400
```

priya.kapoor: interesting — Triton higher throughput for short workloads but worse p95 for long seqs?

sam.greene: exactly. Hypothesis: Triton kernels optimize small-matmul paths and vectorization better for short tokens; flashv3 shines when attention op dominates (long sequences + kv-cache reuse).

jess.lee: any quantization differences? q5/q4?

sam.greene: ran q5 sweep too. Flashv3 q5 gave similar latency to q8 but improved throughput a bit; Triton q5 still slightly ahead on small-batch throughput. However q5 artifacts affect log-prob stability for some eval prompts — opened a quick eval run: https://qa.redwood.ai/runs/4821

kai.zheng: what about warmup/microburst behavior — can we safely switch for prod?

sam.greene: we saw more microburst latency spikes in apac with flashv3 when instance was cold — p99 jumps ~1.6x for first 30s of traffic. Applied a small warmup hook (2 dummy requests) and spikes subsided. Also recommend hysteresis: only flip kernel after sustained 10m improvement in rolling 5m windows.

priya.kapoor: any region-specific config suggestions?

sam.greene: region rules I propose:
- us-west & eu-west: default to flashv3 for models >=7B and seq>=1024. Use Triton fallback for small-token, high-qps routes (sync inference).
- apac: keep Triton default for now until warmup automation is in place.
- autoswitch: require >=10k requests and 10m sustained perf delta to switch.

jess.lee: operational concerns? rollback story?

sam.greene: yes — ensure model variant parity (same quant profile). Add canary: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with automatic revert on error rate or p95 degradations >15%. Also keep binary indicator in traces for kernel used.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist reminder: add kernel flag to rollout API, record kernel in span attributes, and add alert for >10% p95 variance post-switch.

kai.zheng: sounds good. Action items for me: (1) add warmup hook automation, (2) implement hysteresis window + metric, (3) prep canary script. Target: staging test by EOD Friday.

priya.kapoor: I'll update the kernel recommendation doc and region playbook and link to your dashboard.

sam.greene: thanks all — will upload full CSVs and perf traces to the bench run later today. :thumbsup:

jess.lee: awesome. tagging @kai so it's on your radar. :rocket:
